section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
section_1.content: Briefly review wave superposition and phase coherence. Explain that light is an electromagnetic wave characterized by amplitude and phase (the 'position' of the wave peak).
section_1.example: Visualizing a ripple in a pond: how two ripples meeting create a complex pattern of peaks and troughs (constructive vs. destructive interference).

section_2.title: Understanding Diffraction
section_2.content: Define diffraction as the bending of waves around obstacles. Introduce the mathematical concept using the Fourier Transform: the diffraction pattern is the spatial frequency representation of the object.
section_2.example: A laser pointer shining through a thin mesh (like a screen door) to produce a grid of dots—the 'diffraction pattern' encodes the shape of the mesh.

section_3.title: The Holography Mechanism: Recording
section_3.content: Explain that while photos only capture intensity (amplitude), holography captures interference patterns. Introduce the 'Reference Beam' vs. 'Object Beam' concept to record phase information.
section_3.example: An animation showing two light waves meeting on a photographic plate, creating a 'frozen' interference pattern that looks like static noise but contains 3D data.

section_4.title: The Holography Mechanism: Reconstruction
section_4.content: Explain that shining the original reference beam back through the developed hologram acts like a 'key,' diffracting the light to recreate the original wavefronts.
section_4.example: Imagine a 3D hologram of a rotating Iron Man helmet: as you walk around the hologram, you see different sides of the helmet because the phase-encoded light reconstructs the original spatial volume.

section_5.title: Synthesis and Applications
section_5.content: Connect the math (Fourier optics) to real-world technology. Summarize how diffraction enables the storage of 3D space on a 2D surface.
section_5.example: Modern applications: Holographic data storage for long-term archival or high-security authentication on credit cards.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Offset to align correctly in the right-side layout
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Applications", [
            "Fourier optics explain holographic storage.",
            "We map 3D space to 2D.",
            "Technology secures credit card data."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        hologram_icon = VGroup(
            Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3),
            Circle(color=TEAL, radius=0.5)
        )
        data_cloud = VGroup(*[Dot(color=GREEN) for _ in range(10)])
        lock_icon = VGroup(
            Rectangle(color=YELLOW, height=0.6, width=0.5, fill_opacity=0.2),
            Circle(color=YELLOW, radius=0.2).shift(UP*0.3)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
